draft.title: How endings shape interpretation
card: An ending is the last part of a text. It gives readers a final view that can change how they understand everything that came before.
the main problems are settled. Readers feel a sense of closure, and the events seem to have led to a clear outcome.
the main question is left unanswered. Readers must decide for themselves what happens or what it means, so more than one reading is possible.
the ending reveals something unexpected. Readers look back and see earlier details in a new way, such as a narrator who was not telling the truth.
draft.remember: The ending is the last thing a reader meets, so it can reshape how they read the whole text.

a.q: A story ends on the day Ravi opens a letter. We are never told what it says or what he does next. What type of ending is this?
a.why: The story stops with the main question unanswered, so readers must decide what the letter means. A twist would reveal something surprising that changes earlier events, but nothing is revealed here.
a.clue: Does the story answer its main question?

b.q: In a story, a calm narrator describes a quiet week at a lighthouse. In the last paragraph we learn she has been alone there for years, and that the visitors she mentioned were never real. How does this ending affect the way readers see the earlier parts?
opts: They reread the visits as signs of her loneliness
They see the earlier parts as unchanged by the ending
They treat the visitors as real and the ending as a mistake
They see the story as unfinished and open to any reading
b.why: This is a twist ending. The reveal makes readers look back and see the visits in a new way, as a sign of her loneliness. The ending is not open, because the story does answer what was real and what was not.
b.clue: What do readers do with earlier details after a surprising reveal?

b.best: They reread the visits as signs of her loneliness
